guide.title: Pain Management
guide.lead: Pain relief is part of good care, not an extra. Measure pain with a scale that fits the patient, use the splint and cold pack before and alongside drugs, reassess after every intervention and write it down. Children, older adults and people with dementia are the most often undertreated.

sections.title: Choose the scale
rows: Adults and older children who can rate it
Children 2 months to 7 years, non-verbal patients
FLACC: face, legs, activity, cry, consolability (each 0–2)
notes: A change of 2 points or more is meaningful.

sections.title: Without drugs
items: Splint the injury; support in position of comfort
Gentle handling and a smooth ride

rows.note: Oral; avoid in kidney disease, bleeding
Not for pneumothorax, bowel obstruction, decompression illness

groups.title: Opioids
items: Monitor respiratory rate, SpO₂, EtCO₂ and sedation

groups.title: Fractures
items: Mid-shaft femur: traction splint helps pain
Hip fracture: padded immobilisation (pillows, vacuum mattress, scoop); no traction splint

groups.title: Document
items: Scale, scores, drug, dose, route, time, reassessment

quiz.q: A 6-year-old with a forearm fracture can't rate pain in numbers. Best scale?
quiz.explanation: FACES works from 3 years; FLACC is for those who can't self-report.

quiz.q: Pain falls from 8 to 5 after splinting. This means:
options: A meaningful improvement: the splint is working
An alert woman in labour who can hold the mouthpiece
A child who can't hold the mask
quiz.explanation: It expands gas pockets and needs self-administration.

quiz.q: Hip fracture in an 82-year-old. Immobilise with:
options: Padded immobilisation: pillows, vacuum mattress or scoop
quiz.explanation: Traction splints are for mid-shaft femur fractures.

quiz.q: Before giving an opioid, have ready:
quiz.explanation: Watch breathing, SpO₂, EtCO₂ and sedation.

quiz.q: Who is most often undertreated for pain?
options: Children, older adults and people with dementia

flashcards.question: Numeric rating scale
flashcards.answer: 0–10: mild 1–3, moderate 4–6, severe 7–10. A change of 2 points or more is meaningful.

flashcards.question: Wong-Baker FACES
flashcards.answer: Faces scale for children 3 years and older, or limited language: the patient points to a face.

flashcards.question: FLACC
flashcards.answer: Face, legs, activity, cry, consolability, each 0–2: for children 2 months to 7 years and non-verbal patients.

flashcards.question: Non-drug pain relief
flashcards.answer: Splint, cold pack wrapped in cloth, position of comfort, reassurance, distraction, gentle handling.

flashcards.question: Methoxyflurane
flashcards.answer: Self-administered inhaled analgesic: 3 mL, maximum 6 mL per day. Not with kidney impairment, malignant hyperthermia history or reduced consciousness.

flashcards.question: Nitrous oxide contraindications
flashcards.answer: Pneumothorax, bowel obstruction, decompression illness, head injury with reduced consciousness, inability to self-administer.

flashcards.question: Barriers to good analgesia
flashcards.answer: Undertreatment of children, older adults, people with dementia and minority groups; bias; language barriers; protocol limits.

flashcards.question: Documenting analgesia
flashcards.answer: Scale, scores before and after, drug, dose, route, time, side effects, response.

critical.scenario: A 4-year-old fell from the monkey bars; her forearm is angulated and she won't let anyone touch it. Her mother asks you to do something for the pain.
critical.question: Assessment and management?

options.t: FACES score, distraction and reassurance, well-padded splint with gentle handling, wrapped cold pack, analgesia per protocol, reassess with FACES
Too young to assess: splint fast and go
options.f: Children from 3 years can use FACES.
Splint in the position found unless the circulation is compromised.

critical.explanation: Intranasal fentanyl 1.5 mcg/kg is one option per protocol.
critical.kpi: Appropriate paediatric pain assessment using age-validated tool with multi-modal management

critical.scenario: An 82-year-old with dementia fell: right leg shortened and externally rotated, moaning and flinching when anyone approaches. She can't use a number scale.
critical.question: Best pain approach?

options.t: FLACC score, padded immobilisation (pillows, vacuum mattress, scoop), cold pack, gentle handling, analgesia per protocol, reassess FLACC
No pain score, so no analgesia

critical.explanation: People with dementia are often undertreated; FLACC lets you measure and reassess.
critical.kpi: Uses FLACC scale for pain assessment in a non-verbal elderly patient with dementia

critical.scenario: A 28-year-old with an isolated closed mid-shaft femur fracture, alert, pain 9/10. After several breaths of methoxyflurane his pain is 6/10. He asks to use it more.
critical.question: Next step?

options.t: Let him keep self-administering (up to the daily maximum), apply a traction splint, cold pack, reassess and document
Take the inhaler away: it has done all it can

options.f: A traction splint is one of the best pain treatments here.

options.t: Give methoxyflurane and nitrous oxide together, unmonitored

critical.explanation: Combining drugs and splinting works better than either alone; ALS can add IV analgesia.
critical.kpi: Combines pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for multi-modal pain management
